name: SenseiDB
tagline: LinkedIn's distributed, real-time faceted-search database on Lucene, Zoie and Bobo; archived since 2014.
description: SenseiDB was a distributed, elastic database for semi-structured data that LinkedIn built and open-sourced around 2010, and which powered parts of the LinkedIn homepage and the LinkedIn Signal product. It combined Lucene for full-text search, Zoie for real-time indexing and Bobo for fast faceted browsing, sharded and replicated across nodes coordinated by ZooKeeper, and offered BQL, an SQL-like language with MATCH ... AGAINST, GROUP BY and BROWSE BY facets. Data streamed in through gateways for Kafka, JDBC, JMS and files, or was bootstrapped from HDFS with a MapReduce indexing job. Development stopped after the 1.5.x releases around 2012-2013, and LinkedIn archived the repository; Elasticsearch and OpenSearch cover the same ground today.
statusNote: Development ended around 2013 and LinkedIn's repository is archived (LinkedInAttic). Use Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or Apache Solr.

scale.notes: Sharded and replicated across nodes with ZooKeeper; replicas converge eventually.

strengths: Real-time indexing: updates searchable within moments of arriving
Fast faceted browsing via Bobo alongside full-text relevance
SQL-like BQL with facets, grouping and full-text predicates
Ingest gateways for Kafka, JDBC and JMS plus Hadoop bootstrapping
Proven at LinkedIn scale in its day
weaknesses: Archived and unmaintained for over a decade
Built on old Lucene versions with no upgrade path
useCases: Historical reference for real-time faceted search architecture
Migrating legacy Sensei deployments to Elasticsearch or OpenSearch
